key_insight: A symmetry-adapted single-orbital tight-binding model can reproduce the band-edge dispersions and spin splittings of chiral 1D hybrid perovskite (R/S-PEA)PbI3 using only a small set of spin-dependent hopping terms.
engineering_relevance: This gives device modelers a compact, interpretable Hamiltonian for predicting spin, optical, and transport behavior in chiral lead-halide perovskites relevant to solar-cell and spintronic design.
method: Build a single-orbital effective Hamiltonian on four symmetry-related sites per primitive unit cell.
Include layer, in-plane sublattice, and spin degrees of freedom with separate parameter sets for conduction and valence bands.
Use symmetry analysis with screw eigenvalues and antiunitary operators to distinguish accidental from symmetry-enforced degeneracies.
evidence_signal: The model is validated against density-functional-theory band structures and shown to quantitatively capture band-edge spin splittings and leading Bloch-state spin-polarization patterns.
watch_item: Because the Hamiltonian is fitted with separate conduction/valence parameters and focuses on low-energy states, its transferability away from the band edges or to altered compositions/structures may be limited.
paper_title: Single-orbital tight-binding model for chiral one-dimensional hybrid organic-inorganic lead halide perovskites
